rationale: Buy 12.00 USDT of spot at 76,994.5 and leave futures flat. This is a staged redeployment of the cash the endday raised, not a new directional bet, and the size is deliberately about one third of the free cash. The endday sold roughly 15.00 USDT at 78,035.1 on a correct bearish call; price is now 1,040.6 points and 1.33 percent lower, so buying part of it back here is what raising the cash was for. The level is chosen rather than picked at random: the measured liquidation shelf sits directly underneath, with 678,769 USD of longs force-sold at 76,800 across 43 fills and 470,401 USD at 76,700 across 49, all between 08:02Z and 08:12Z, and the 76,704 low held two minutes after the largest single print of 395.95 contracts at 76,716.9. Price has spent the three hours since holding 290.5 points above that low with three flat hourly closes of 76,997.0, 76,980.6 and 77,050.1, and the only short liquidations of the session printed on the way back up at 77,123 to 77,188. The 15m MACD has crossed with the histogram at plus 46.49 and 15m RSI has repaired from 22.22 at the low to 40.45. Monday's US spot ETF row also completed at plus 159.9 million, ending the four-session outflow streak that totalled minus 462.7 million. The reason the size is small rather than full is the other half of the data and it should not be buried: open interest is 2,165,293,019.18 USD, UP 5.32 percent from the 2,055,912,361.89 the endday read, so about 109 million USD of notional was ADDED while price fell, and the long-short account ratio has climbed without a break from 1.22 at 00:00Z to 1.73 at 11:00Z. Accounts are catching this knife with new leverage, which is the exact configuration the endday identified as dangerous and was right about. Price is also 128.1 points below the 77,122.6 daily EMA20 on a live bar that will not settle until 19:00 COT, and the FOMC lands tomorrow with a hike priced above 85 percent and the US 10-year at a 52-week high of 5.00 percent. So: a real tranche into a real shelf, with 23.38 USDT held back for the flush that a crowded long book usually produces. Futures stay flat because taking leverage into an FOMC against 1.73 crowding is a coin flip, not an edge.

message.text: You are 25 minutes behind me because this session fired at 06:25 COT instead of 02:00, so treat my read as your starting point rather than as stale overnight context. Two numbers decide your call. First, whether the 76,704 low holds - I deployed 12.00 USDT against it and left 23.38 dry, so if a settled 1H close prints below it you inherit a losing tranche and the right move is to stop adding, not to average it. Second, the long-short account ratio: I read 1.73 at 11:00Z after an unbroken climb from 1.22. If it is still rising when you check and price has not recovered the 77,122.6 daily EMA20, the queue of longs has not cleared and nothing I did should be scaled up. If it has started to fall while price holds, that is the emptied-book setup and the remaining cash is there for it.

lesson.pattern: A one-sided liquidation flush is only a reversal signal when open interest and the long-short account ratio BOTH fall through it. Falling open interest with a falling ratio means the crowded side actually left. Falling price with rising open interest and a rising ratio means the crowd is being replaced at a worse price, and the flush is a stop on the way down rather than a floor.
lesson.insight: The 13 September midnight session learned that an emptied book is a reversal setup, and that lesson has now been misapplied once and correctly refused once. The 14 September endday refused it - it saw the ratio climbing 1.20, 1.21, 1.22 through the flush and stayed bearish - and price fell another 1,040.6 points. Overnight the ratio went to 1.73 and open interest ROSE 5.32 percent while price fell, which is the same signal an order of magnitude louder. Record the ratio as a required second condition on the flush rule, not as a footnote to it.
